name: Road Trip Checklist
description: A complete road trip planning checklist covering route and stops, packing, snacks, entertainment and pre-departure prep.

items.text: Map your full route with start and end points
Mark fuel, food, and rest stops along the way
Book overnight lodging or campsites in advance
Download offline maps and directions
items.note: Cell service can drop on rural and mountain roads.

items.text: Check the weather and road conditions for your route
Share your itinerary and arrival times with someone at home
Plan scenic detours or attractions you want to see
Driver's license and vehicle registration
Proof of insurance
Reservation confirmations for lodging and attractions
Cash and a debit or credit card
Roadside assistance membership card and number
ID for each traveler
Phone mount and charging cables
Power bank and a 12V car charger
Sunglasses and a sunshade for parked stops
Reusable water bottles for everyone
Trash bag and a roll of paper towels
Tissues, wet wipes, and hand sanitizer
Basic first-aid kit
Outfits for the length of the trip plus one spare
Comfortable shoes and a layer for cooler evenings
Toiletries and any medications
A small day bag kept in the cabin
items.note: Pack what you need at stops so you avoid digging through the trunk.

items.text: Pillow and a light blanket for passengers
Reusable shopping bag for purchases along the way
Trail mix, nuts, and dried fruit
Granola or protein bars
Crackers, chips, or pretzels
Fresh fruit that travels well, like apples and grapes
Jerky or cheese sticks
Water and a few caffeinated drinks for the driver
A small cooler with ice packs for perishables
Road trip playlist and offline music
Audiobooks and podcasts downloaded ahead
Downloaded shows or movies on a tablet
Travel games and a deck of cards
Books or magazines for passengers
Headphones for each traveler
Fill the fuel tank the night before
Check tire pressure and the spare tire
Top off fluids and washer fluid
Confirm the route and first stop with everyone
Lock up the house and adjust the thermostat
Charge all phones and devices fully

faq.q: How do I plan a road trip route?
faq.a: Map your start and end points, then mark fuel stops, meals, and overnight stays roughly every two to three hours of driving. Build in extra time for breaks and detours, and save an offline copy of the route in case you lose signal.

faq.q: What should I pack for a road trip?
faq.a: Pack clothing for the trip length, a small bag of car essentials within reach, phone chargers, snacks and water, and any documents you need. Keep a separate day bag in the cabin so you do not have to dig through the trunk at every stop.

faq.q: What snacks are best for a road trip?
faq.a: Choose mess-free, non-perishable snacks like trail mix, granola bars, fruit, crackers, and jerky, plus plenty of water. Keep them in an easy-to-reach bag or small cooler so the driver and passengers can grab a bite without stopping.

faq.q: Can I print this road trip checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item as you plan your route and pack the car.

faq.q: How do I keep kids entertained on a road trip?
faq.a: Pack downloaded shows and music, audiobooks, travel games, and a few small surprises to reveal during long stretches. Plan stops at parks or attractions so everyone can stretch and burn off energy.
